facts: AstroMLab 5 is a research project led by Yuan-Sen Ting.
The project involves approximately 400,000 astrophysics papers.
Collaborating institutions include The Ohio State University and Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics.
The goal of AstroMLab 5 is to create structured summaries and extract key concepts.
The dataset includes 408,590 astrophysics papers from arXiv.
It spans the years 1992 to July 2025.
The dataset contains 3.8 million paper-concept associations.
The concept vocabulary and embeddings are available on GitHub.
Large language models are capable of reasoning about scientific literature and executing complex retrieval tasks.
The authors created a centralized dataset of 408,590 arXiv astronomy papers.
The dataset includes 9,999 unique concepts along with semantic embeddings.
Astronomy literature often lacks adequate text curation and controlled vocabularies like the Unified Astronomy Thesaurus.
Converting astrophysics PDFs to machine-readable text requires OCR rather than LaTeX source files.
The pipeline initially employed Nougat, which required approximately 1 minute of V100 GPU processing per paper.
Starting November 2024, the team transitioned to Mathpix OCR API due to superior reliability.
Inspection of Mathpix-processed pages showed no systematic errors affecting summary quality.
The summarization approach processes academic papers by splitting them into ~10,000-character segments.
The method emphasizes the retention of LaTeX formulas and excludes acknowledgments and references.
The complete summarization involved 408,590 papers and cost over $50,000 in API fees.
Raw summaries are reorganized into seven semantic sections for structured knowledge representation.

The authors use large language models GPT-4o and o1-mini to extract approximately 10 key concepts per research paper. They employ K-means clustering with k=10,000 on embedded concept descriptions to ensure consistency across papers. The final vocabulary was refined to 9,999 concepts distributed across eight categories. The category with the most concepts is Cosmology & Nongalactic Physics, which has 2,192 concepts.
ADS keywords suffer from severe sparsity, with 44% of papers having 3 or fewer keywords.
The most common ADS keyword, "galaxies: evolution," appears in 16,321 papers.
The proposed extraction method achieves an average of 9.4 concepts per paper.
The median concept frequency for the proposed method is 223 papers, compared to 28 for ADS keywords.
Temporal analysis tracks concept emergence over three decades using a 5-paper threshold for stability.
A notable peak in new concept emergence occurred in 2007 due to arXiv's cross-listing policy expansion.
From 2015 to 2025, deep learning concepts like CNNs and transformers dominate new concepts in astrophysics.
Comparing 1992-2003 and 2023-2025 shows that computational domains have evolved from peripheral to core components in astrophysics research.
The dataset covers all astro-ph papers from 1992 through July 2025.
The dataset includes concept embeddings generated using text-embedding-3-large.
The citation network contains 1.67 million unique identifiers.
Structured summaries follow a conservative distribution policy detailed in the appendix.
The dataset contains 408,590 astrophysics papers from arXiv spanning the years 1992 to 2025.
There are 9,999 AI-generated concepts included in the dataset.
The average number of concept associations per paper is 9.4.
The dataset tracks the emergence of machine learning in astrophysics post-2015.
The document describes a structured summary framework for academic papers in astrophysics from 2015 to 2025.
The case study focuses on USco1606-1935, a candidate wide low-mass triple star system.
The analysis uses 2MASS archival data and spectroscopy from Palomar Observatory.
190 emergent astrophysics concepts appeared between 2015 and 2025, representing approximately 2% of total vocabulary.
